text:
maya: Heads-up — saw a flurry of OOMs on prod pool-gpu-7 during the 11:00 traffic spike. KV cold-starts + long sequences. Heap/allocator patterns look like repeated workspace reallocation.
oliver: saw the alerts. stack traces point at kernel selection switching from fast-f32 to quantized-kernel when sequence > 1024. memory footprint jumps ~1.4x. :frowning:
henry: KV cache miss storm is amplifying the problem — many concurrent requests hit an empty shard, we pull large KV buffers into workspace at once.
saniya: TL;DR: cold KV + aggressive kernel switch = workspace fragmentation and OOM. we should have a multipath mitigation: short-circuit KV, throttle, and reuse buffers while we stabilize.
maya: proposal (quick):
- enable short-circuit for KV fetch path for 30s after an OOM spike (return warm fallback or compressed embeddings)
- hold allocator arena resizing for in-flight requests (1.25x cap on workspace growth)
- force kernel to stable-fallback (slower but memory-friendly) for requests queued > 100ms
- add temporary leaky-bucket throttle at ingress to keep batch sizes smaller
oliver: agree. also suggest adding a fast, low-mem kernel-selection override flag we can flip without a deploy: `runtime.override_kernel=stable_low_mem`
henry: runtime-bot: can we add a short-lived circuit-breaker rule that routes requests matching long_seq=true to model-128q or to host fallback?
runtime-bot: noted. Circuit-breaker template created: `cbid:cb-rapid-kv-01`, rule: if OOM rate > 0.5% over 1m AND kv_miss_rate > 20% route long_seq -> model-128q (quantized, lower workspace). Applies to pool-gpu-7. :white_check_mark:
saniya: small code snippet for ingress throttle (pseudo):
```
if inflight_requests > 120:
  accept = random() < 0.7  # 70% pass-through, 30% retry-after
else:
  accept = true
```
maya: for buffer reuse: pin a small pool of reusable tensors per-worker. when allocating workspace, try `pop()` from pool before new alloc. keep lifetime <= 60s to avoid stale growth.
oliver: can we add live profiling markers so we can see if kernel switch is the culprit vs allocator fragmentation? put `profiling.tag("kernel_switch")` before selector and `profiling.tag("kv_pop")` on KV pulls.
henry: I'll roll a canary config with all mitigations to staging (kv short-circuit + override_kernel + buffer_pool=on + ingress throttle). deploy-bot: canary started — cfg://canary/rapid-kv-mitigation-2026-03-18
deploy-bot: canary instances: 4 -> healthy checks passing
maya: monitoring checklist:
- add temporary dashboard: OOM rate, kv_miss_rate, avg_workspace_bytes, kernel_switch_rate, inflight_requests
- set alert if avg_workspace_bytes > baseline * 1.25 for >2m
saniya: post-mortem notes to include: why kernel heuristics switch at 1024 triggers large allocations, add regression test with mixed sequence lengths and simulated KV-thundering herd.
oliver: after canary looks good, we'll flip cbid:cb-rapid-kv-01 for prod pools and leave override_kernel as a toggle for 24h, then roll back if perf regressions.
henry: running the canary load test now (locust). will post logs in 10m.
maya: thanks — also add a quick eval: token-per-dollar for model-128q vs stable kernel so we can communicate cost tradeoffs to SRE/product.
henry: load test results: 10m run — OOMs eliminated, avg_latency +18% for long sequences, cost delta ~ -12% (due to quantized model). Posting histograms in the channel shortly.
oliver: good tradeoff for emergency mitigation. we should follow up with longer-term fixes: kernel autotuner that considers aggregate KV pressure and a smarter allocator that can compact arenas.
saniya: +1. I'll open a tracking ticket with proposed work: AUTOTUNE-kerneled-allocator and link this thread. :spiral_note_pad:
maya: 👍 closing loop once we promote to prod and monitor for 6 hours. thanks all.
